law_name: Act amending the Constitution of the Republic of Estonia (Eesti Vabariigi põhiseaduse muutmise seadus): voting rights in local elections
description: Adopted by the Riigikogu as a matter of urgency on 26 March 2025 by 93 votes to 7. It revokes the right of third-country nationals living in Estonia to vote in municipal elections and, from the elections after 2025, that of stateless residents (holders of the 'grey passport'), leaving the vote to Estonian and EU citizens. President Alar Karis promulgated it, saying MPs had taken 'a decision with very serious consequences' and urging a clear path to citizenship for loyal long-term residents.
significance: A government priority pushed by Michal, aimed mainly at Russian and Belarusian citizens; the October 2025 municipal elections were the first held under it.

law_name: Act amending the Churches and Congregations Act (kirikute ja koguduste seadus)
description: Government bill passed on 9 April 2025 by 60 votes to 13. Churches, congregations and monasteries in Estonia may not be directed by, or linked by statutes or financially to, a foreign religious centre or leader that poses a threat to Estonia's security or constitutional or public order; the aim was to separate the Estonian Christian Orthodox Church from the Moscow Patriarchate. President Karis twice refused to promulgate it, calling it disproportionate and unconstitutional (Indrek Tarand in Postimees); in October 2026 Karis said the matter had been resolved in the Supreme Court and that the law had been signed.
significance: One of the most disputed security laws of the Michal government; according to the Kyiv Independent, the Riigikogu had designated the Russian Orthodox Church an 'institution sponsoring the military aggression of the Russian Federation' on 6 May 2024.

law_name: 2025 State Budget Act and the fixed-term security tax package
description: Approved by the cabinet in September 2024 and submitted by Michal to the Riigikogu: €5.6 billion for military defence over four years, defence spending of at least 3.3% of GDP a year, Ukraine aid of 0.25% of GDP, a nominal deficit of 3% of GDP, spending cuts of €1 billion over four years and a 10% cut in public-sector spending over three years. It introduced a fixed-term security tax until 2028 (VAT up two points in mid-2025; 2% on personal income and corporate profits from 2026), capped sickness and parental benefits, ended state social-tax payments for stay-at-home parents and reformed unemployment benefits from 2026.
significance: Michal promised 'tax peace' until 2027 with this package; the corporate and personal-income parts of the security tax were later dropped (2025).

law_name: Income tax changes in force from 2026: flat €700 basic exemption ('tax hump' abolished); security tax and 24% rate cancelled
description: From 1 January 2026 every taxpayer has a basic exemption of €700 a month (€8,400 a year) that no longer decreases with income, ending the 'tax hump'. The 2% security tax on personal income and company profits did not take effect and the planned rise of the income tax rate to 24% was cancelled, so the rate stays at 22%, according to 2026 tax guidance citing the Ministry of Finance and the Tax and Customs Board. The abolition of the tax hump had been legislated in 2023 for 2025 and was postponed by one year in 2024.
significance: Delivered Reform's main 2023 tax pledge; together with other cuts it lowers the projected tax burden from 36.6% to 35.2% of GDP in 2026.

law_name: Act amending the Motor Vehicle Tax Act and the Traffic Act (family reduction)
description: Passed by the Riigikogu on 12 November 2025: the car tax of a parent or guardian of a child under 18 who owns an M1 or N1 vehicle is reduced by up to €100 per child for each taxation period; the taxation period is shortened when a vehicle is removed from the register; 8- and 9-seat minibuses are taxed and registered at the lower N-category rates.
significance: Implemented the May 2025 Reform–Estonia 200 coalition pledge on the car tax.

description: Approved by the Riigikogu by 51 votes to 37: revenue of €18.6 billion and expenditure of €19.5 billion, investments of €1.3 billion (45% more than in 2025), €780 million less tax revenue, the overall tax burden down from 36.6% to 35.2% of GDP, a deficit of 4.5% of GDP and debt rising to 25.9% of GDP (Via Baltica, citing ERR).
significance: The Reform–Estonia 200 government's main pre-election budget, combining tax cuts with record defence spending.

law_name: Agreement between Estonia and Sweden on the enforcement of Swedish prison sentences in Tartu Prison (prison rental agreement)
description: Signed in Stockholm in June 2025 and ratified by the Riigikogu on 10 June 2026, together with the implementing amendments: up to 600 inmates from Sweden may serve their sentences in Tartu Prison, selected with the Police and Border Guard Board, the Internal Security Service and the interior ministry, and returned to Sweden before the end of their sentence. Expected to bring at least €30–60 million in revenue and keep Tartu Prison open; the first inmates were due in August 2026.
significance: A first lease of Estonian prison capacity to another EU state, negotiated by Michal's government.
